newsitem.title: GERMANY: German construction industry hard-hit by recession.
newsitem.headline: German construction industry hard-hit by recession.

text.p: The German construction industry has been hard-hit by the recession which has triggered a dramatic rise in bankruptcies in east German states, an industry association said on Tuesday.
The Hauptverband der Deutschen Bauindustrie said the unemployment rate among German construction workers has jumped 32 percent since June 1995, with the rate rising by 47.5 percent in east Germany.
The association said in June 1996 that 186,000 construction workers were unemployed with 67,000 unemployed in east German states.
Association President Otmar Franz said that employers' decision to cancel existing wage contracts last week was the only choice the group had and likened it to pulling the emergency brake on a car.
He said he hoped the move would allow the association and the union to quickly work out a new wage contract.

The group last week cancelled two contracts which promised east German workers a 1.85 percent pay rise on September 1 and promised to lift their salaries to 95 percent of west German workers' wage levels from the current 92 percent ratio on October 1.
But Franz was optimistic that workers would not strike, as they had threatened to.
The association said firms wanted to freeze eastern wages at current levels for the coming year and urged the IG Bau building union to start talks on a new agreement as soon as possible.
Construction demand has crumbled in west and east Germany, registering eight percent below year ago levels in June, the group said.
In total the group said 1,000 companies have declared bankruptcy in the first half of this year, the group added.
